title: Attestation dry-run scratch: control traces & open questions
content:
Purpose: quick, messy brain-dump for the feb/mar 2026 attestation dry-run. Not a final plan — capture ideas, edge cases, and small playback tasks we can run in the next 2 weeks.

Topline goals:
- run a scoped dry-run of ~6 controls end-to-end (identity, change mgmt, logging, incident, backup, access reviews, encryption-at-rest).
- produce oneEvidenceSnapshot per control that an external assessor could interpret without 1:1 hand-holding.
- validate sampling rules and evidence TTL logic (what do we actually keep for 90 days vs 1 year).

Quick control list (pick 6):
1) Identity lifecycle (SC-1-ish): onboarding/offboarding evidence, SSO audit events, ephemeral creds revocation playbook.
2) Change control (PR -> prod): git commit -> CI -> deploy -> audit trail, rollback.
3) Logging/monitoring: ingestion -> retention -> alert -> on-call paging (pager handoff evidence).
4) Backup + restore: snapshot taken, stored, restoration test (small DB restore).
5) KMS & key usage: KMS access policy changes, key rotation record, CMK usage logs.
6) Access reviews: manager attestations captured, stale membership removals.

Playback tasks / artifacts to generate (brainstorm):
- tiny scripted scenario for identity: create temp user in IdP (okta staging), grant role, log in, run api action, then deprovision; capture okta logs + internal onboarding ticket + slack approval thread (screenshot).
- change control: open a feature PR (staging only), run pipeline until deploy, trigger a canary rollback; capture GitHub PR, CI logs (build + deploy timestamps), deployment manifest diffs.
- logging: trigger synthetic error from staging backend, validate it appears in Datadog (or internal log store), export alert runbook + paging message and acknowledgment timestamp.
- backup restore: take a small RDS snapshot, restore to dev namespace and run smoke tests; collect snapshot id, restore job logs.
- KMS: rotate a key in staging KMS, capture KMS audit log entries.
- access review: run the quarterly access query, export CSV, create review ticket, capture manager approval emails and user deprovision entries.

Evidence heuristics / minimal artifact list per control (what assessor needs):
- identifier (ticket/PR/hash) + human-readable summary (1-2 lines)
- timeline (timestamps in ISO) for all key events
- who (user id / principal) + role / justification where relevant
- immutable log link or snapshot (hash + storage URI)
- supporting docs: screenshots, policy excerpt, runbook version
- retention policy reference: where is this stored and for how long (storage class + TTL)

Open questions (need answers before dry-run):
- Evidence authenticity: do we stamp artifacts with a deterministic hash and store a manifest? (pros: easier to prove integrity; cons: new work for tooling).
- Redaction policy: PII in screenshots/logs — can we auto-mask, or do we hand redact? What counts as redaction proof?
- Cross-system correlation: timestamps drift between Okta, GitHub Actions, and internal infra. How tolerant do assessors expect us to be? Edge: clocks off by >30s.
- Sampling: for some high-volume controls (alerts), we will sample 1 week vs full 90 days. Need to define sampling rationale and randomization seed.
- Evidence TTLs: S3 lifecycle vs cold archive — do we point assessors to archive retrieval steps or surface a short-lived snapshot in warm storage?

Small implementation notes / one-off scripts to build:
- evidence-manifest.sh: given a list of artifact URIs, output JSON manifest with SHA256s and signed timestamp (GPG?)
- playback-harness (python): uses staging creds to exercise the control flows and collect artifacts to a temp Evidence bucket (s3://redwood-attest-dryrun/{run-id}/)
- redact-helper: small CLI to scan logs for emails/SSNs and replace with [REDACTED:pattern-#] and annotate what was changed. Keep original encrypted in cold store.

Assessor-friendly packaging idea:
- each control gets a folder: /evidence/{run-id}/{control}/manifest.txt + artifacts/* + narrative.md (2–3 paragraphs: scope, steps executed, why this proves control).
- narrative template: "Scope: ...; Steps executed: ...; Observed outputs: ...; Notes/limitations: ...; Owner: ..."

Runbook fragment (for on-call/ops assisting the dry-run):
- PR for DryRun: create branch dryrun/attest-<date> with scripts + README
- Slack channel: #attest-dryrun (invite SRE, infra sec, ci owner, compliance rep)
- Timebox: 1.5 hours per control for execution + 1 hour for packaging + 1 hour for assessor walkthrough
- Failure handling: if any step missing artifact, capture a "failed-evidence" note explaining what we would do in prod and why artifact missing.

Notes from 1:1s / fragments I scribbled:
- Arjun mentioned: we could leverage existing cost-optimized cold bucket for originals and surface pre-signed short-lived artifact in warm bucket. Need a policy for pre-signed expiry length (>72h?)
- Ellie: redaction is the pain — let's AVL a small PII regex set and always store original encrypted with access tag "attest-dryrun".
- Compliance asked: how to handle third-party vendor attestations (e.g., infra provider)? Put vendor cert in evidence folder and link version/date.

Risks / gotchas to call out early:
- Shared staging environment: extra noise from unrelated teams will pollute traces. We should coordinate a short quiet-window for runs or use dedicated ephemeral namespaces.
- Human evidence (manager attestations) are slow — we should create pre-approved mock attestations for dry-run and clearly mark them as mock.
- Clock sync: ensure run nodes use NTP; add a step to capture ntpstat output in manifests.

Immediate TODO (next 48h):
[ ] pick final 6 controls and owners (ask SRE, InfraSec, Compliance)
[ ] create staging run-id + S3 bucket prefix and minimal IAM role for evidence-collection (least privilege)
[ ] write evidence-manifest.sh prototype and test hash outputs
[ ] draft narrative template and example for identity control
[ ] schedule 2-hour dry-run session with stakeholders (include assessor rep if possible)

Longer-term (post-dry-run):
- bake evidence-manifest generation into CI for retention controls so future audits are incremental.
- iterate sampling rationale and publish a short rationale doc for assessors.

Random thought: could we automate a physical "attestation binder" export (zip) with sign-off page (PDF) that includes a tamper-evident checksum? Might make external assessment faster.

Scratch lines / fragments:
- "proof_of_hash: s3://redwood-attest-dryrun/manifest-{id}.sha256"
- example SQL to pull access reviewers: SELECT user, last_seen, manager, membership_source FROM team_members WHERE last_seen < now() - interval '90 days';
- quick grep for login: grep 'LOGIN_SUCCESS' /var/log/auth.log | tail -n 200

If anyone reading: add anything obvious I missed on the slack thread #attestation-dryrun. I'll try a prototype manifest later today and ping for quick review.

---
